Description: Smooth scrolling only for anchor links on long pages, never under reduced motion
Do: Use scroll-behavior: smooth inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), for anchor links only
Don't: Smooth-scroll every navigation or ignore reduced motion
Code Example Bad: html { scroll-behavior: smooth; } with no reduced-motion guard

Description: Fixed nav should not obscure content
Do: Add padding-top to body equal to nav height
Don't: Let nav overlap first section content

Description: Current page/section should be visually indicated
Do: Highlight active nav item with color/underline
Don't: No visual feedback on current location

Description: Users expect back to work predictably
Do: Preserve navigation history properly

Description: URLs should reflect current state for sharing
Do: Update URL on state/view changes

Description: Show user location in site hierarchy
Do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth

Description: Motion only answers an action or shows what changed
Do: Animate in response to an action (open, save, move) or to show a change
Don't: Decorative entrances, staggered reveals or looping decoration
Code Example Good: Motion on open/save; one orchestrated first-screen moment (B2C)
Code Example Bad: animate-bounce or fade-up on every section

Description: Motion duration depends on distance complexity platform and user context
Do: Use shared motion tokens and test that feedback stays responsive
Don't: Present 150-300ms or any cutoff as a universal requirement
Code Example Bad: One duration copied to every transition

Description: Respect user's motion preferences
Do: Check prefers-reduced-motion media query

Description: Show feedback during async operations
Do: Use skeleton screens or spinners
Don't: Leave UI frozen with no feedback

Description: Hover effects don't work on touch devices
Do: Use click/tap for primary interactions
Don't: Rely only on hover for important actions

Description: Infinite animations are distracting
Do: Use for loading indicators only

Description: Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
Do: Use transform and opacity for animations

Description: Easing should match how an element changes speed and purpose
Do: Use deceleration when arriving acceleration when leaving and linear for constant-rate progress
Don't: Reject linear easing even for steady rotation or progress
Code Example Good: ease-out for entry; linear for spinner

Description: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements
Do: Define z-index scale system (10 20 30 50)

Description: Hidden overflow can clip important content
Do: Test all content fits within containers

Description: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible
Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Code Example Good: Fixed nav + fixed bottom with gap

Description: New stacking contexts reset z-index
Do: Understand what creates new stacking context
Don't: Expect z-index to work across contexts

Description: Images badges validation text and skeleton replacements can shift nearby content when they update
Do: Reserve appropriate space or keep async states in a stable content-driven container
Don't: Insert compact text or media without a layout strategy
Code Example Good: aspect-ratio for media; stable count slot for badges

Description: 100vh can be problematic on mobile browsers
Do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome

Description: Content too wide is hard to read
Do: Limit running text to 50-75 characters per line (about 70ch)
Don't: Let text span full viewport width

Description: Adjacent touch targets need adequate spacing
Do: Minimum 8px gap between touch targets

Description: Custom gestures can conflict with system
Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content

Description: 300ms tap delay feels laggy
Do: Use touch-action CSS or fastclick

Description: Keyboard focus, including controls inside a modal, needs a visible indicator
Do: Use a visible focus ring on every interactive control, including modal controls

Description: Interactive elements react to hover; non-interactive ones do not
Do: Pointer cursor and a visual change, instant or within 150 ms, on interactive elements only
Don't: No hover feedback on clickable elements, or animated hover on non-interactive cards
Code Example Bad: No hover style, or hover:scale on a static card

Description: Show immediate feedback on press/click
Do: Add pressed/active state visual change

Description: Clearly indicate non-interactive elements
Do: Reduce opacity and change cursor

Description: A submit button stays enabled until the request starts, then ignores repeat presses
Do: Keep it enabled until the request starts; while it runs show progress and ignore repeat presses (a busy state, not the disabled attribute)
Don't: Allow a second submission, or disable the button before the user tries
Code Example Good: aria-busy={loading} + spinner; repeat clicks ignored while loading
Code Example Bad: disabled before submit; a second click sends twice

Description: Users need to know when something fails
Do: Show clear error messages near problem

Description: Confirm successful actions to users
Do: Show success message or visual change

Description: Guard destructive actions by reversibility
Do: Undo for reversible actions; a confirmation naming the object and the consequence for irreversible ones
Don't: Confirm everything (people stop reading) or delete irreversibly without confirmation
Code Example Good: Undo toast for archive; confirmation dialog for permanent delete
Code Example Bad: Are-you-sure on every action; permanent delete on one click

Description: Text must be readable against background
Do: Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text

Description: Don't convey information by color alone
Do: Use icons/text in addition to color

Description: Images need text alternatives
Do: Descriptive alt text for meaningful images

Description: Screen readers use headings for navigation
Do: Use sequential heading levels h1-h6
Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling

Description: Interactive elements need accessible names
Do: Add aria-label for icon-only buttons

Description: Web users need complete keyboard navigation with visible focus on every operable control
Do: Keep tab order aligned with visual order and test every action without a pointer
Don't: Keyboard traps or illogical tab order

Description: Content should make sense when read aloud
Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly

Description: Inputs must have associated labels
Do: Use label with for attribute or wrap input

Description: Field errors are announced politely; failed operations assertively
Do: Tie a field error to its field with aria-describedby and announce it politely; role=alert only for a failed operation
Don't: Visual-only errors, or role=alert on every field error
Code Example Good: <input aria-describedby='email-error'> + polite message; role='alert' for a failed request
Code Example Bad: Red border only, or role='alert' on every field error

Description: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation
Do: Provide skip to main content link
Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages

Description: Large images slow page load
Do: Use appropriate size and format (WebP)

Description: Load content as needed
Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content

Description: Large bundles slow initial load
Do: Split code by route/feature

Description: Repeat visits should be fast
Do: Set appropriate cache headers
UX Rule: не применяем: конфиг nginx в deploy-topology следует эталону

Description: Web fonts can block rendering
Do: Use font-display swap or optional

Description: External scripts can block rendering
Do: Load non-critical scripts async/defer

Description: Large JavaScript slows interaction
Do: Monitor and minimize bundle size

Description: CSS/JS can block first paint
Do: Inline critical CSS defer non-critical

Description: Every input needs a visible label
Do: Always show the label above the input

Description: Each invalid field needs an inline error connected to that field
Do: Show a specific error below the input and reference it with aria-describedby
Don't: Show only a top-level error without identifying each invalid field

Description: Validate on blur, never while typing
Do: Validate on blur and again on submit; clear the error as soon as the value is fixed
Don't: Validate on every keystroke, or only on submit

Description: Use appropriate input types
Do: Use type email, tel or url and inputmode numeric or decimal; never type number

Description: Help browsers autofill correctly
Do: Use autocomplete attribute properly

Description: Mark fields by product type
Do: B2B: (необязательно) on optional fields only; B2C: * on required and (необязательно) on optional
Don't: Leave fields unmarked, or mark them differently across screens
Code Example Bad: Unmarked fields, or mixed marking across screens

Description: Let users see password while typing
Do: Toggle to show/hide password

Description: Confirm form submission status
Do: Show loading then success/error state

Description: Inputs should look interactive
Do: Use distinct input styling
Don't: Inputs that look like plain text

Description: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
Do: Use inputmode attribute

Description: Design and build the desktop width first; the narrow width must work
Do: Start from the main (desktop) width in the frames register and adapt down; test the narrow width
Don't: Ship a narrow width that breaks or loses actions
Code Example Good: Desktop default + max-width queries for the narrow width, both tested

Description: Test at all common screen sizes
Do: Test at every width in the frames register, desktop first

Description: Mobile layouts need touch-sized targets
Do: Increase touch targets on mobile

Description: Text must be readable on all devices
Do: Minimum 16px body text on mobile

Description: Set viewport for mobile devices
Do: Use width=device-width initial-scale=1

Description: Avoid horizontal scrolling
Do: Ensure content fits viewport width

Description: Images should scale with container
Do: Use max-width: 100% on images

Description: Tables can overflow on mobile
Do: Use horizontal scroll or card layout

Description: Adequate line height improves readability
Do: Use 1.5-1.75 for body text

Description: Long lines are hard to read
Do: Limit to 50-75 characters per line

Description: Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
Do: Use consistent modular scale

Description: Fonts should load without layout shift
Do: Reserve space with fallback font

Description: Body text needs good contrast
Do: Use darker text on light backgrounds

Description: Headings should stand out from body
Do: Clear size/weight difference

Description: Loading feedback should match the expected wait and avoid flashing for near-instant work
Do: Follow platform and component guidance; preserve layout focus and accessible busy status
Don't: Apply one timing threshold to every operation or leave long waits unexplained
Code Example Good: Stable skeleton or progress with aria-busy

Description: Guide users when no content exists
Do: Show helpful message and action

Description: Help users recover from errors
Do: Provide clear next steps

Description: Show progress for multi-step processes
Do: Step indicators or progress bar

Description: Toasts are for success only
Do: Success only, one at a time, 4-10 seconds, role=status; errors stay until resolved
Don't: Errors in a toast, or toasts that vanish before they can be read
Code Example Bad: Error message in a toast that disappears

Description: Confirm successful actions
Do: Brief success message

Description: Handle long content gracefully
Do: Truncate with ellipsis and expand option

Description: Use locale-appropriate date formats
Do: Use relative or locale-aware dates

Description: Format large numbers for readability
Do: Use thousand separators or abbreviations

Description: Show realistic placeholders during dev
Do: Use realistic sample data
UX Rule: процесс ui-design: в макетах реалистичные данные

Description: Users should be able to skip tutorials
Do: Provide Skip and Back buttons

Description: Help users find results faster
Do: Show predictions as user types

Description: Dead ends frustrate users
Do: Show 'No results' with suggestions

Description: Editing one by one is tedious
Do: Allow multi-select and bulk edit

Description: Users need to know they talk to AI
Do: Clearly label AI generated content

Description: Waiting for full text is slow
Do: Stream text response token by token

Description: Autoplaying media consumes data and creates motion barriers
Do: Prefer click-to-play; provide pause and captions; stop off-screen and honor reduced motion
Don't: Auto-play high-resolution loops without pause or captions

Description: AI needs user feedback to improve
Do: Thumps up/down or 'Regenerate'

Description: Parallax/Scroll-jacking causes nausea
Do: Honor prefers-reduced-motion and present the final readable state without parallax or scroll-jacking

Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires keyboard focus to remain at least partially visible
Do: Offset sticky UI with scroll-padding and dismiss or move persistent overlays
Don't: Let headers footers banners or chat widgets fully cover focus

Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a single-pointer alternative for author-controlled drag operations
Do: Add buttons menus or tap-to-move controls and retain keyboard operation
Don't: Make dragging the only way to reorder resize or select
Code Example Good: Move up and Move down buttons beside drag handle

Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires 24 CSS px pointer targets or an applicable exception
Do: Use at least 24 by 24 CSS px or verify spacing equivalent inline user-agent or essential exceptions
Don't: Assume native 44pt or 48dp guidance defines web conformance

Description: WCAG 2.2 A requires repeated help mechanisms to stay in the same relative order
Do: Keep contact self-help and automated help in consistent locations
Don't: Move help controls to different locations on each page

Description: WCAG 2.2 A avoids requiring the same information twice in one process
Do: Auto-populate prior values or let users select previously entered information
Don't: Ask users to retype the same address or account data without necessity

Description: WCAG 2.2 AA says authentication must not depend only on a cognitive function test unless an exception applies
Do: Allow password managers and paste; offer passkeys OAuth or another non-cognitive method
Don't: Block paste or require manual OTP transcription with no alternative

Description: Auto-rotating content needs user control
Do: Provide previous next and play/pause; stop on focus or hover and when reduced motion is requested
Don't: Auto-advance slides without a stop control

Description: An error summary for failed validation complements inline field errors and must be easy to find by keyboard and screen reader users
Do: Place it at the top of the form; move focus to it after a failed submit; link each item to its field; keep the inline errors. A one-field form keeps focus on the field instead
Don't: Replace inline errors with a visual-only summary or move focus on every blur
Code Example Good:
There is a problem

Enter an email address
Code Example Bad: Toast only with no field links or focus target

Description: Short multi-line headings may use balanced wrapping as a progressive visual heuristic
Do: Bound the measure and test natural-wrap fallback across widths fonts and locales
Don't: Promise an exact final line or insert blanket nonbreaking spaces or hardcoded br tags
Code Example Bad: Heading copy rewritten with forced last-line breaks

Description: URLs identifiers and user content must not force horizontal overflow
Do: Use overflow-wrap anywhere and let flex or grid text children shrink
Don't: Apply word-break break-all to all prose

Description: Text must remain available at narrow widths zoom and user spacing overrides
Do: Use fluid sizes content-driven height and unitless line height
Don't: Clip text in fixed-width or fixed-height boxes

Description: Headings actions errors safety text and distinguishing names need complete access
Do: Wrap stack resize or provide a visible full-detail path
Don't: Clamp essential meaning only to make cards uniform
Code Example Good: Action label wraps or opens full details
Code Example Bad: Primary action shown only as an unexplained ellipsis

Description: Badges communicate state while chips or tags represent values or actions
Do: Choose static or interactive markup from the label's meaning and ownership
Don't: Make every pill clickable or encode status with color alone

Description: Filter chips and editable value collections must preserve labels when space or text size changes
Do: Wrap the collection or use an operable +n disclosure for hidden overflow values
Don't: Force all chips into one clipped row or hide overflow values

Description: A badge chip or pill label should stay whole on one line when practical and disclose unavoidable truncation
Do: Bound only unpredictable values; use nowrap with a shrinkable label; expose full text to keyboard pointer and touch users
Don't: Let one compact label wrap to a second line or use a hover-only tooltip
Code Example Good: Flexible label with min-width 0 and an operable full-value disclosure
Code Example Bad: Fixed-width badge wraps to second line or clips with title-only recovery

Description: Interactive chips need a native role accessible name state keyboard operation and visible focus
Do: Prefer a button and expose pressed or selected state that matches the visible label
Don't: Use a clickable div or reveal the only action on hover

Description: Async badge and count changes should announce a meaningful contextual status without moving focus
Do: Use one appropriate atomic status message such as 3 items in cart
Don't: Announce a bare number or make every badge a competing live region

Description: Rapid compact-control changes can interrupt an in-flight transition
Do: Cancel or replace prior motion; set the final semantic state directly and handle cancellation cleanup
Don't: Depend on animationend or transitionend for required state correctness
Code Example Bad: Enable the chip only inside transitionend
